description: The bare word DEFAULT as a DML value writes the column's DECLARED default: NULL for a column without one (refused only by a NOT NULL constraint, as a NULL), the next sequence value for AUTOINCREMENT; it works positionally, per row of a multi-row VALUES, in UPDATE SET and in both MERGE clauses - and it is a marker ONLY where it stands alone, resolving as an invalid identifier inside any larger expression. Converted 1:1 from dml/DefaultMarkerTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dm (a INT DEFAULT 9, b INT, c INT NOT NULL, s VARCHAR(5) DEFAULT 'x')
INSERT INTO dm (a, b, c, s) VALUES (DEFAULT, DEFAULT, 1, DEFAULT)
SELECT a, b, c, s FROM dm
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dm (a INT DEFAULT 9, b INT, c INT NOT NULL, s VARCHAR(5) DEFAULT 'x')
INSERT INTO dm (a, b, c, s) VALUES (1, 2, DEFAULT, 'y')

error.messageContains: failed on column C with error: NULL result in a non-nullable column

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dms (k INT, v INT DEFAULT 3)
MERGE INTO dms t USING (SELECT 1 AS k) s ON t.k = s.k WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (k, v) VALUES (s.k, DEFAULT)
SELECT k, v FROM dms
MERGE INTO dms t USING (SELECT 1 AS k) s ON t.k = s.k WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.v = DEFAULT
SELECT k, v FROM dms
